about.title: Personal Injury Help in Lomita, California
about.longDescription: Lomita is a small, tight-knit city in Los Angeles County, but its streets still carry a steady flow of traffic — much of it funneling through Pacific Coast Highway, Western Avenue, Lomita Boulevard, and Palos Verdes Drive N. Public records show 29 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, leaving 36 people hurt and, tragically, 1 person dead. Those aren't abstract numbers if you or someone you love was one of them. Maybe you were stopped at a light on Western Avenue when someone rear-ended you, or you were crossing Lomita Boulevard when a driver failed to yield. Whatever happened, the days after a crash are often filled with pain, paperwork, and uncertainty about what comes next. We're here to help. Our team handles personal injury cases in Lomita and can review your situation, explain your options, and answer your questions at no cost. There's no obligation, and if we take your case, you won't owe legal fees unless there's a recovery. You've got enough to deal with; let us help you carry some of that weight.

whyChoose.title: What You Should Know Before You Wait

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California law generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it pays to act sooner rather than later.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't End It
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Unlike some states, California doesn't cap non-economic damages — like pain and suffering — in ordinary injury cases, which matters when an injury changes your daily life.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless You Win
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost. Legal fees only come out of a settlement or judgment if your case succeeds.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Lomita?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If your claim involves a government agency or public road authority, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your situation early.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, so being partially at fault doesn't stop you from recovering compensation. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of responsibility.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Lomita?
items.answer: Public crash records show that Pacific Coast Highway, Western Avenue, Lomita Boulevard, and Palos Verdes Drive N. see the highest volume of reported collisions in the city, with activity often peaking on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m. These are neutral collision counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Do you charge anything to review my case?
items.answer: No. Our initial consultation is free. We work on contingency, meaning we don't charge upfront fees. If we take your case, legal fees come only from a settlement or judgment if you recover compensation.

items.question: What kind of compensation might be available for pain and suffering?
items.answer: California doesn't place a cap on non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in standard personal injury cases. We can review your specific injuries and circumstances to explain what might apply to your situation.
